yarn-dinkum.meaning: Every instruction and all code, markup and links intact: the _projects_ suggestion, both command sets, the underscore convention ("So it’s _hello_world.rs_, not _helloworld.rs_"), `.\main` on Windows, the Troubleshooting pointer, the welcome.
yarn-dinkum.sense: Terms fit: "Rust couldn’t care less", "chuckin’ all yer projects in there", "punch in" for typing commands, "the usual go" for convention, "have a squiz", "get a hand", "good on ya!".
yarn-dinkum.authenticity: Natural: "Righto, first thing ya do", "Got more than one word in yer filename?", "welcome to the club!".
yarn-dinkum.register: Aussie throughout in a friendly spoken voice, but no swearing and no yarning asides: a confident level 4 rather than 5.
yarn-dinkum.tone: Keeps the tutorial's warm, encouraging tone: "If `Hello, world!` came up, good on ya!"
yarn-dinkum.flow: Reads like it was written that way: "Save it and head back to yer terminal window".
yarn-dinkum.variety: Good: "Righto", "fire up", "punch in" (three times), "chuckin’", "stick", "squiz", "good on ya".
yarn-dinkum.essence: Unmistakably the Rust book's Hello World section.

yarn-troppo.meaning: Every instruction and all code kept. Asides hang off the original: "could be under the house with the redbacks for all it cares", "which looks like a sneeze", "cos Windows always has to be different", "First round’s on you." Colour, not new facts.
yarn-troppo.sense: "doesn’t give a flyin’ toss" for 'doesn't matter', "whack an underscore", "nip back", "No dramas.", "Easy as." all fit.
yarn-troppo.authenticity: Mostly natural ("the usual go", "No dramas. Have a squiz back"), but "Strewth, where do I start?" and "Fair dinkum." are stock tags.
yarn-troppo.register: A full level-5 yarn with swearing inside the dial: "ya poor bugger", "every bloody one of ’em", "a flyin’ toss".
yarn-troppo.tone: Stays warm and encouraging, but the cheek leans past the tutorial's even voice ("And if yer stuck with Windows CMD, ya poor bugger"); still friendly.
yarn-troppo.flow: Lively and readable; "Strewth, where do I start? With a directory, that’s where: somewhere to keep yer Rust code." is a clunky opening, and short tags ("Fair dinkum.") interrupt.
yarn-troppo.variety: Wide range: "fire up", "punch in", "whack", "crack open", "nip back", "No dramas", "Easy as", "squiz", "redbacks".
yarn-troppo.essence: Recognisably the tutorial, steps intact, retold with jokes; its plain helpfulness is a little crowded.

unharnessed.meaning: All instructions and code intact; "Welcome aboard, mate!" keeps the welcome.
unharnessed.sense: "couldn't give a toss", "punch in", "chuck in this" for entering commands, "the done thing", "have a squiz", "you bloody legend" fit; "chuck in" for typing commands strains slightly.
unharnessed.authenticity: Mostly natural; "we reckon you make a _projects_ directory" is an awkward construction (reckon you should).
unharnessed.register: Light-to-moderate Aussie, mostly standard "you" and the book's own sentences ("Next, make a new source file and call it _main.rs_."); "bloody legend" the only swear. About level 3.
unharnessed.tone: Tutorial tone kept, warm close: "good on ya, you bloody legend!"
unharnessed.flow: Smooth, but the parallel "chuck in this:" lines repeat stiffly.
unharnessed.variety: Some range: "First up", "give a toss", "punch in", "chuck in", "done thing", "squiz"; "chuck in this" twice.

yarn-deadset.meaning: All instructions and code intact; "Say, use _hello_world.rs_, not _helloworld.rs_."
yarn-deadset.sense: "doesn’t give a toss", "the usual go", "have a squiz", "good on ya" fit.
yarn-deadset.authenticity: Natural but thin; "Say, use" is slightly American.
yarn-deadset.register: Moderate: ya/yer and a few terms on the book's sentences; no swearing beyond "toss". About level 3.
yarn-deadset.tone: The tutorial's tone intact: "That makes ya a Rust programmer—welcome!"
yarn-deadset.flow: Readable but "punch in" in nearly every instruction makes it drone.
yarn-deadset.variety: "punch in" leaned on ("punch in these commands", "punch in this", "punch in this", "punch in the code", "punch in these", "punch in the command").

engine.sense: Only g-drops and "yer"; nothing to misfit.
engine.authenticity: Contractions inserted mechanically: "directory'n a directory", "created'n enter", "compile'n run"; otherwise the book's American prose.
engine.register: Largely untranslated: "Regardless of your operatin' system", "refer back to the". Far below level 5.
engine.tone: The tutorial's tone kept, being the tutorial.
engine.flow: The 'n joins and mixed "yer"/"your" ("go back to your terminal window") jar.
engine.essence: The original, nicked by odd contractions.

summaries.yarn-dinkum: A natural, friendly Aussie tutorial that keeps every instruction and all code; a notch under full level 5.
summaries.yarn-troppo: The full level-5 yarn, varied and faithful, with a few stock tags and extra cheek.
summaries.unharnessed: A lightly Aussie, accurate tutorial; under the level-5 brief.
summaries.yarn-deadset: Accurate and natural but light, and leans hard on 'punch in'.
summaries.engine: The original with mechanical g-drops and 'n contractions; far off the brief.
